source: Mobile Canvas metadata-only tools/list; no device operations invoked.

tools.name: mobile_device_app_install
tools.title: Install app
tools.description: Install an app from a host path: a .app bundle on iOS, an .apk on Android. Use this to put a freshly built app on the device without leaving the session.

path.description: Host path to a .app bundle (iOS) or .apk file (Android).

tools.name: mobile_device_app_launch
tools.title: Launch app
tools.description: Launch an app by bundle ID (iOS) or package name (Android). Prefer this over tapping a home screen icon: it does not depend on where the icon sits or whether it is on the first page.

bundleId.description: Bundle ID on iOS, package name on Android.

relaunch.description: Stop the app first, so this is a cold start rather than a bring-to-front.

tools.name: mobile_device_app_list
tools.title: List installed apps
tools.description: List the apps installed on a device, with bundle ID (iOS) or package name (Android), version, and whether each is running. Built-in system apps are excluded unless includeSystem is set, because they outnumber a developer's own apps many times over.

text.description: Filter by bundle ID or display name; substring and case-insensitive.

limit.description: Maximum number of apps to return.

tools.name: mobile_device_app_op_list
tools.title: List Android app operations
tools.description: Report the app operations an Android app is subject to -- the permissions that never appear in a runtime prompt, such as SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, WRITE_SETTINGS and REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES. uidScoped marks a mode set for the whole uid, which overrides the package's own. Android only; on iOS use permission_list.

tools.name: mobile_device_app_op_set
tools.title: Change an Android app operation
tools.description: Put one app operation into a mode, to reach behaviour behind a special-access screen without walking Settings to get there. Modes: allow, deny, ignore (refused silently), default. The mode is read back, because appops accepts a change for an operation the app never declared and drops it while reporting success. Android only.

mode.description: One of allow, deny, ignore, or default.

tools.name: mobile_device_app_terminate
tools.title: Terminate app
tools.description: Stop a running app. Its data is left alone; only the process ends.

bundleId.description: Bundle ID on iOS, package name on Android.

tools.name: mobile_device_app_uninstall
tools.title: Uninstall app
tools.description: Uninstall an app and delete its data. This is destructive and cannot be undone, so it requires confirm to be set.

bundleId.description: Bundle ID on iOS, package name on Android.

confirm.description: Must be true; the app's data is deleted with it.

tools.name: mobile_device_battery_set
tools.title: Simulate a battery state
tools.description: Simulate a charge level or charging state, to reach low-power behaviour and charging-only code paths. On iOS this is a status bar override, so it is also how a screenshot gets a fixed battery indicator.

state.description: One of charging, discharging, or full.

tools.name: mobile_device_biometric
tools.title: Present a biometric scan
tools.description: Present a fingerprint or face scan that the device either accepts or rejects, to drive an unlock prompt without any hardware. A rejection is the path worth testing, because it is the one apps most often leave unhandled. On Android the emulator confirms it took the event. On iOS it cannot: the scan is posted to a notification bus that reports nothing back, so 'confirmed' comes back false and the result has to be read from the app itself. The device must already have a biometric enrolled, which is a device setting rather than something this can turn on.

action.description: Either match to accept the scan, or nomatch to reject it.

fingerId.description: Which enrolled finger to present, on Android. Ignored on iOS.

tools.name: mobile_device_boot
tools.title: Boot virtual device
tools.description: Boot a device, wait until it is ready, and return its updated deployment record.

tools.name: mobile_device_call
tools.title: Ring, answer or end a call
tools.description: Ring the device from a number, or answer, hold or hang up a call already in progress, then read the call list back. Android only. Placing a call needs a number; the other actions apply to the call in progress when no number is given. An incoming call is the classic interruption an app has to survive -- it takes audio focus and moves the app to the background.

action.description: One of place, accept, hold, or cancel.

number.description: The other party's number. Required to place a call, optional afterwards.

annotations.title: Ring, answer or end a call

tools.name: mobile_device_calls
tools.title: List phone calls
tools.description: List the calls the device's telephony stack currently knows about, with the platform's own state for each such as RINGING or ACTIVE. Android only.

tools.name: mobile_device_catalog
tools.title: Get device catalog
tools.description: Get installed runtimes and system images, device types, devices, capabilities, and dependency diagnostics for every supported platform.

tools.name: mobile_device_clipboard_get
tools.title: Read the pasteboard
tools.description: Read what is on the device's pasteboard. iOS only -- the Android emulator cannot reach its clipboard from outside, and says so rather than returning an empty string that would look like an empty clipboard.

tools.name: mobile_device_clipboard_set
tools.title: Write the pasteboard
tools.description: Put text on the device's pasteboard and read it back, so a paste-into-field flow can be driven without typing. iOS only. Note that the Simulator can be set to share its pasteboard with the host Mac, in which case the host can overwrite what is written here.

text.description: The text to place on the pasteboard.

tools.name: mobile_device_crash_report
tools.title: Read crash report
tools.description: Read one crash report in full, using an ID from mobile_device_crashes.

tools.name: mobile_device_crashes
tools.title: List crash reports
tools.description: List crashes and ANRs the device recorded, newest first. These survive the app that produced them, so this finds failures that happened while nothing was watching. Pass an ID from here to mobile_device_crash_report for the full stack.

text.description: Filter by process name or bundle ID; substring and case-insensitive.

tools.name: mobile_device_create
tools.title: Create virtual device
tools.description: Create and boot a hidden iOS simulator or Android emulator from an installed runtime/system image and device type returned by mobile_device_catalog.

name.description: Display name for the new device.

runtimeId.description: Runtime identifier from the device catalog.

deviceTypeId.description: Device type identifier from the device catalog.

tools.name: mobile_device_delete
tools.title: Delete virtual device
tools.description: Permanently delete a device. Requires confirm=true.

confirm.description: Must be true to authorize permanent device deletion.

tools.name: mobile_device_display
tools.title: Get device display geometry
tools.description: Get the display geometry of a booted device: logical point size, pixel size, scale, and orientation. Call this before tapping or swiping so coordinates land where intended; all input takes logical points, not pixels.

tools.name: mobile_device_erase
tools.title: Erase virtual device
tools.description: Permanently erase all content and settings from a device. Requires confirm=true.

confirm.description: Must be true to authorize permanent data erasure.

tools.name: mobile_device_file_delete
tools.title: Delete a file or directory
tools.description: Remove a file or directory from the device. Use it to reset one fixture without clearing all of an app's data, which is what uninstalling or wiping would do. Deleting a directory needs recursive, so a mistyped path cannot take a subtree with it. A path that does not exist is an error rather than a quiet success.

path.description: Path to remove; relative to the app container when bundleId is set.

bundleId.description: Scope the path to this app's data container.

recursive.description: Required to delete a directory and everything inside it.

tools.name: mobile_device_file_list
tools.title: List device files
tools.description: List a directory on a device. With bundleId the path is relative to that app's data container -- where its database, preferences and written files live -- and without it the path is an absolute device path. Prefer bundleId: it is stable across reinstalls, where the container's own path is not.

bundleId.description: Scope the path to this app's data container.

path.description: Directory to list; relative to the app container when bundleId is set.

tools.name: mobile_device_file_mkdir
tools.title: Create a directory
tools.description: Create a directory on the device, along with any missing parent. Use it to prepare a place to push a file into, since a push fails when the destination directory does not exist. A directory that already exists is fine.

path.description: Directory to create; relative to the app container when bundleId is set.

bundleId.description: Scope the path to this app's data container.

tools.name: mobile_device_file_pull
tools.title: Pull file from device
tools.description: Copy a file off the device onto this machine, so it can be opened or inspected here. Use it for the database or log an app wrote. An existing file at the destination is overwritten.

path.description: File to copy; relative to the app container when bundleId is set.

output.description: Where to write it on this machine. A directory takes the file's own name.

bundleId.description: Scope the path to this app's data container.

tools.name: mobile_device_file_push
tools.title: Push file to device
tools.description: Copy a file from this machine onto the device, so an app can read it. Use it to place a fixture or a seeded database. An existing file at the destination is overwritten.

input.description: File on this machine to copy.

path.description: Destination; relative to the app container when bundleId is set.

bundleId.description: Scope the path to this app's data container.

tools.name: mobile_device_get
tools.title: Get virtual device
tools.description: Get one virtual device and its native UDID, state, runtime, display, and capabilities.

tools.name: mobile_device_get_selected
tools.title: Get selected canvas device
tools.description: Get the device selected by one canvas panel, including the UDID suitable for deployment commands. Returns hasSelection=false when the canvas has not chosen a device yet.

sessionId.description: Copilot session ID that owns the canvas.

tools.name: mobile_device_hardware_get
tools.title: Read simulated hardware state
tools.description: Read the simulated battery and network state. The 'unreadable' list names what this platform will not report, which is the difference between a value that is absent and one that is zero.

tools.name: mobile_device_list
tools.title: List virtual devices
tools.description: List local mobile virtual devices across iOS simulators and Android emulators, running ones first, with exact deployment identifiers.

tools.name: mobile_device_location_clear
tools.title: Clear the simulated location
tools.description: Return an iOS simulator to the host's real position. An Android emulator cannot do this -- it has no position of its own to return to -- and says so.

tools.name: mobile_device_location_set
tools.title: Set the simulated location
tools.description: Move the device to a latitude and longitude, to exercise location-dependent behaviour without going there. Neither platform can read a location back, so confirm it through the app under test rather than by reading the device. On Android the fix only reaches an app that is already listening for location: the emulator pushes the position to live listeners rather than storing it, and reports success either way, so set the location after the app has started requesting it.

tools.name: mobile_device_log
tools.title: Read device log
tools.description: Read recent log output from a device. Filter to one app with bundleId and to the lines that matter with level, both of which filter on the device rather than afterwards: an idle simulator writes tens of thousands of lines a minute. Levels are verbose, debug, info, warning, error and fatal; Apple's log has no warning rung, so asking iOS for warning yields errors and faults.

bundleId.description: Limit to one app's process, by bundle ID (iOS) or package name (Android).

level.description: Drop anything quieter than this: verbose, debug, info, warning, error, fatal.

text.description: Filter by message text; substring and case-insensitive.

seconds.description: How far back to read, in seconds.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return, newest first.

tools.name: mobile_device_long_press
tools.title: Long press device
tools.description: Press and hold a booted device at logical point coordinates, for context menus, drag handles, and icon rearrangement.

tools.name: mobile_device_media_add
tools.title: Add photos or videos
tools.description: Copy images or videos from this machine into the device's photo library, so a photo picker or upload flow has something to find. Works on both platforms. iOS also accepts vCard files, which land in Contacts.

paths.description: Absolute paths on this machine to the files to add.

tools.name: mobile_device_network_set
tools.title: Simulate network conditions
tools.description: Slow the connection down, to exercise timeouts, spinners and retry paths. Real only on an Android emulator: an iOS simulator shares the host's network, so this only changes what its status bar shows, and the result reports that as networkIsIndicatorOnly. Profiles, slowest first: gsm, gprs, edge, umts, hsdpa, lte, full.

latencyMs.description: Added round-trip latency in milliseconds; 0 removes it. Android only.

tools.name: mobile_device_notification_push
tools.title: Send a push notification
tools.description: Deliver a simulated remote push notification to an installed app, so notification handling can be exercised without a server or a signing certificate. iOS only: the Android emulator has no equivalent, and reaching an Android app this way means sending it a real FCM message. The payload is APNs JSON and must contain an 'aps' key, for example {"aps":{"alert":{"title":"Hello","body":"World"}}}. The app must already have been granted notification permission, which only happens when the app itself asks; this reports that rather than reporting a delivery iOS silently dropped.

bundleId.description: The bundle ID of the app to notify. It must already be installed.

payload.description: The APNs payload as JSON, 4096 bytes or less, containing an 'aps' key.

tools.name: mobile_device_permission_list
tools.title: List app permissions
tools.description: Report the permissions an app holds. Granted is null when the platform will not say -- on iOS an app that has never been asked has no record, which is not the same as denied.

bundleId.description: Bundle ID or Android package name of the app.

tools.name: mobile_device_permission_set
tools.title: Grant or revoke a permission
tools.description: Grant, revoke, or reset one permission, so a permission-dependent screen can be reached without answering a system prompt by hand. Reset makes the app ask again next time. Names that work on both platforms: camera, microphone, location, location-always, contacts, calendar, reminders, photos, photos-add, media-library, motion, notifications. A platform's own name also works. The result reports what actually changed, read back from the device.

bundleId.description: Bundle ID or Android package name of the app.

action.description: One of grant, revoke, or reset.

tools.name: mobile_device_presentation_get
tools.title: Read status bar overrides
tools.description: Report whether the status bar is fixed for screenshots, and with what. On iOS the values themselves come back; on Android only whether it is on, because SystemUI will confirm that and nothing more -- readable says which you got.

tools.name: mobile_device_presentation_set
tools.title: Fix the status bar for screenshots
tools.description: Pin the clock, battery and signal so a screenshot taken now matches one taken next month -- otherwise every capture carries the wall clock and whatever the battery happened to be. Set enabled false to put the real values back. Fields left unset keep what they were showing, so a second call can adjust one of them. The change is confirmed against the device: both platforms accept these and silently ignore them under conditions this reports rather than hides.

enabled.description: True to fix the status bar, false to restore the device's own values.

time.description: Clock as 24-hour HH:mm, such as 09:41. Redrawn in the device's own format.

batteryCharging.description: Whether to draw the charging bolt.

carrierName.description: Carrier name beside the signal bars. Sent to both platforms, but iOS cannot report it back so it is absent from the returned overrides, and devices with a notch have no room to draw it at all.

hideNotifications.description: Android only: hide the notification icons. iOS does not draw them here.

annotations.title: Fix the status bar for screenshots

tools.name: mobile_device_press_button
tools.title: Press device button
tools.description: Press a hardware button on a booted device. iOS accepts home, lock, side-button, siri, and apple-pay; Android accepts home, back, apps, power, volume-up, volume-down, and menu.

button.description: Button name. iOS: home, lock, side-button, siri, apple-pay. Android: home, back, apps, lock/power, volume-up, volume-down, menu.

tools.name: mobile_device_press_key
tools.title: Press key
tools.description: Press one USB HID keyboard key on a booted device.

keyCode.description: USB HID keyboard usage code, such as 40 for Return or 42 for Backspace.

tools.name: mobile_device_recording_start
tools.title: Start device recording
tools.description: Start a bounded H.264 MP4 screen recording on a booted device.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum recording duration in seconds, from 1 through 3600.

outputPath.description: Optional absolute output path; omit to use the Mobile Canvas artifacts directory.

tools.name: mobile_device_recording_status
tools.title: Get recording status
tools.description: Get current screen-recording status and output metadata for a device.

tools.name: mobile_device_recording_stop
tools.title: Stop device recording
tools.description: Stop and finalize the active device recording, returning its persistent output path.

tools.name: mobile_device_restart
tools.title: Restart virtual device
tools.description: Shut down and boot a device, waiting until it is ready.

tools.name: mobile_device_reveal
tools.title: Reveal virtual device
tools.description: Show a virtual device window. Reveals an iOS simulator in its selected Xcode host app; restarts a headless Android emulator with its native window.

tools.name: mobile_device_rotate
tools.title: Rotate device
tools.description: Rotate a booted device to a new orientation.

orientation.description: Target orientation: portrait, portrait-upside-down, landscape-left, or landscape-right.

tools.name: mobile_device_screenshot
tools.title: Capture device screenshot
tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot from a booted device and return it as MCP image content.

tools.name: mobile_device_select
tools.title: Select canvas device
tools.description: Select a virtual device for one canvas panel and return its complete deployment target record.

sessionId.description: Copilot session ID that owns the canvas.

tools.name: mobile_device_settings_get
tools.title: Read device settings
tools.description: Read the device's appearance and accessibility text settings.

tools.name: mobile_device_settings_set
tools.title: Change device settings
tools.description: Switch dark mode or scale up text, to check a layout under conditions a user will hit. Settings left unset are left alone. Text size differs by platform: iOS takes a named contentSize such as 'large' or 'accessibility-extra-large', Android takes a numeric fontScale such as 1.3.

fontScale.description: Android text scale, where 1.0 is the default.

contentSize.description: iOS content size category, or 'increment'/'decrement' to step one.

increaseContrast.description: Turn the increase-contrast accessibility setting on or off.

tools.name: mobile_device_shutdown
tools.title: Power off virtual device
tools.description: Power off a device without deleting or erasing it.

tools.name: mobile_device_sms_send
tools.title: Deliver a text message
tools.description: Deliver an inbound text message, as though it arrived over the network. Android only: an iOS simulator has no messaging stack. Useful for one-time-code flows and for interrupting the app under test with a notification it does not control.

tools.name: mobile_device_swipe
tools.title: Swipe device
tools.description: Swipe or drag across a booted device using logical point coordinates and a duration.

tools.name: mobile_device_tap
tools.title: Tap device
tools.description: Tap or long-press a booted device at logical point coordinates.

duration.description: Press duration in seconds; zero performs a tap.

tools.name: mobile_device_type_text
tools.title: Type text
tools.description: Type text into the focused control on a booted device, using clipboard paste for unsupported Unicode.

text.description: Text to enter into the focused control on the device.

tools.name: mobile_device_ui_dump
tools.title: Read screen elements
tools.description: Read the accessibility hierarchy of whatever is on screen, as a tree of elements with labels, identifiers, roles and logical-point frames. Use this to understand a screen without a screenshot.

includeRaw.description: Also return the untouched platform payload; useful when the normalized tree omits something.

tools.name: mobile_device_ui_find
tools.title: Find screen elements
tools.description: Find on-screen elements by visible text, accessibility identifier, or role. Returns each match with its center point, so the result can be fed straight to a tap.

text.description: Visible text or accessibility label to match; substring and case-insensitive unless exact is set.

role.description: Element role: button, text, field, image, switch, slider, link, cell, list, tab, checkbox, container, other.

exact.description: Require the whole value to match rather than a substring.

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return.

tools.name: mobile_device_ui_tap
tools.title: Tap element
tools.description: Tap the first element matching a query. Prefer this over coordinate taps: it reads the live hierarchy, so it stays correct when layout, scroll position, or device size changes.

text.description: Visible text or accessibility label to match; substring and case-insensitive unless exact is set.

role.description: Element role, for example button, field, or switch.

exact.description: Require the whole value to match rather than a substring.
